rv.q: It's a Fantasticks for the longtime fans, and a warm invitation to the uninitiated to forgive its slight corniness and succumb to its gentle charms.
The director, Christopher Gattelli, manages to make this switch to two boys and their mothers not only feel like the most natural thing in the world
They, and everything else in this production, work together to bring a theatrical warhorse galloping into 21st Century Broadway, surprising us with just how much pluck it can still carry.
Act I hits all its marks here, deftly balancing tenderness, sweetness and humor.
Mr. Gattelli has cast the production with such a wealth of talent that even the fable-phobic can take sustained pleasure in the many wonderful things it does indeed bring.
The answer is a resounding yes in the hands of director Christopher Gattelli and an all-around heavenly cast.
I challenge you to name two better actresses for these parts.

This first Broadway revival of “The Fantasticks” is blessed with great singing voices and Nevin Steinberg’s amplification supports them without homogenizing those voices into the current loud-arena sound design that infects the rest of Broadway.

, director Christopher Gattelli spread large-scale charm through witty ensemble storytelling. It’s a delight to see him working on a smaller canvas now, finding comic chemistry among his cast with a fine brush. He teases a taut screwball dynamic out of Miles and Kritzer that’s part Lucy and Ethel, part Auntie Mame and Vera.
There's more to like in this beautifully sung version of book writer/lyricist Tom Jones and composer Harvey Schmidt's 66-year-old musical making its Broadway debut.
If you haven't, I'd catch it while it makes this brief, welcome return to our boards.

If this quintessential chamber musical may not be the perfect fit for Broadway no matter what the sexual orientation of the characters, at least the gender switch gives such delightful Broadway pros...a chance
The drawback here—it's not meager—is that the boys' love affair comes across as tepid.
Timeless and tender, sentimental and sassy, high-spirited and highly recommended.
Still, you'd have to be a hard-hearted cynic yourself to resist the charms of The Fantasticks .
Gattelli's joyous staging maintains the charm, wit, and warmth of this unimpeachable show, even if the move to a bigger stage at times reminds audiences why it succeeded on more intimate ones.

vs.sum: One of Broadway's smallest houses (597 seats) and one of its newest, built in 2015 as Second Stage's permanent home. The intimate scale means excellent sightlines from nearly every seat, though the modern design prioritizes function over grandeur.

acc.note: Elevator from lower lobby to Mezzanine. LOOP system for t-coils and cochlear implants.
